::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}
# Book_17 — OrgPath at the Network Edge
:::


::: {.callout-note}
The admission plane — RADIUS, 802.1X, and network access control — that Microsoft left to the network. When the domain controller goes away, the AD-bound NPS that decided which device lands on which VLAN goes with it; Intune compliance and Conditional Access both evaluate too late to fill the gap, because they run only after a device already holds a network address. This book binds OrgPath into network admission: the third policy-targeting transport after Intune configuration and Azure Policy workload, carried in the device certificate via EAP-TLS, enforced as VLAN, dACL, TrustSec SGT, and posture at Cisco ISE, Aruba ClearPass, or the Entra RADIUS Proxy, with a bounded hybrid window in which legacy NPS and cloud RADIUS run in paired lockstep until the AAA tier retires. It tells the *why* and the journey; the normative contract is [ADR-073](/docs/adr/adr-073-policy-targeting-nac-third-transport.html), and the operator reference is UIAO_012.
:::
